# PRD: Ardennes Hour

## Summary

A one-hour, two-player WW2 skirmish game whose rules live on the cards. For Sam and one friend. Fifty finished sub-hour games by the end of 2026.

## Problem

Existing skirmish games take an evening because their rules live in a book consulted mid-game. The brief's chain reaches a root cause: the rules are not on the components.

## User

Sam, 38, plays twice a month with one friend, has ninety minutes.

## Success metric and leading indicator

Fifty finished games under sixty minutes reported by 2026-12-31. Leading indicator: three of the first five blind playtests finish without a rules question.

## Scope

Decision: the smaller version, because the metric is about finished games, not content. It keeps one scenario, one deck, two forces. It leaves out the campaign and the third faction. It would still move the number.

## Non-goals

- No solo mode.
- No app companion.

## Requirements

1. Every rule a player needs during a turn is printed on a card in play. Acceptance: a blind playtester completes a full turn without opening any document.
2. A game finishes in under sixty minutes. Acceptance: five of five internal playtests end under sixty minutes on the clock. [C1]
3. The two forces are asymmetric but balanced. Acceptance: across ten playtests neither side wins more than seven. [C2]

## Sequencing and dependencies

Card text before art; balance after five playtests; print after balance.

## Assumptions

- Players will accept cards over dice for activation. [C3]
- The premortem is pending.

## Risks

- Card text too dense to read at arm's length. Mitigation: 12-point minimum, tested on the first print.

## Open questions

- Cards or dice for activation.
